title: Definition of CanvasFilters.filter should define the bounding box of the referencing element
body:
I'm not an expert on filters, so you might want to talk to one of the editors of the [filters spec](https://drafts.fxtf.org/filters/) before resolving this, but:

I think the filters spec depends on the user of filters defining the bounding box of the referencing element.  This is by default used as part of the calculation of the [filter region](https://drafts.fxtf.org/filters/#FilterEffectsRegion) (which is in turn used to calculate the [filter primitive subregions](https://drafts.fxtf.org/filters/#FilterPrimitiveSubRegion)).

If I read the definition of filter region, I think I can make sense of what all of it means based on this wording in the [definition of canvas filters](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html#filters):

> Coordinates used in the value of the filter attribute are interpreted such that one pixel is equivalent to one SVG user space unit and to one canvas coordinate space unit. Filter coordinates are not affected by the current transformation matrix. The current transformation matrix affects only the input to the filter. Filters are applied in the output bitmap's coordinate space.

... except for the part that [says](https://drafts.fxtf.org/filters/#FilterEffectsRegion):

> If filterUnits is equal to objectBoundingBox, then x, y, width, height represent fractions or percentages of the bounding box on the referencing element (see object bounding box units).

It's not clear to me what the "bounding box on the referencing element" is here.  I suspect it would make sense for it to be the size of the canvas (rather than something related to individual drawing operations), but again, you might want to check with a filters expert here.

(I got here from https://github.com/w3ctag/spec-reviews/issues/116 .)
